chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ali Sahib al-Killal, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I was performing Tawaf with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and a man from our companions presented himself to me, asking me to go with him for a need. He gestured to me, and I disliked leaving Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) to go to him. While I was performing Tawaf, he gestured to me again. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saw him and said, 'O Aban, is this one wanting you?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Who is he?' I said, 'A man from our companions.' He said, 'He is upon the same status as you.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So go to him.' I said, 'Should I cut the Tawaf?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And even if it is the Obligatory Tawaf?' He said, 'Yes.'

He said, 'So I went with him, then I returned to him afterwards and asked him, saying, 'Inform me about the right of a believer upon a believer.' He said, 'O Aban, leave it, do not reiterate it.' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you,' but I did not cease reiterating upon him. He said, 'O Aban, would you share half of your wealth with him?'

Then he looked at me and saw what had entered my mind, and said, 'O Aban, do you not know that Allah (Exalted and Majestic) has mentioned those who prefer others over themselves?' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said, 'But when you share half with him, you have not preferred him; rather, you and he are equal. You prefer him only when you give him from the other half.'

key_terms.الْمُؤْثِرِينَ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ: Those who prefer others over themselves

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of preferring a believer over oneself according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the hierarchy of social obligations, where Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prioritizes the immediate need of a companion over the ritual act of Tawaf, even if it is obligatory. It refines the concept of *ithar* (selflessness) by distinguishing between equal sharing (*muqasama*) and true preference, noting that merely splitting wealth in half does not constitute preferring the other over oneself. The Imam clarifies that true *ithar* requires giving more than one's share, aligning with the Quranic praise of those who prioritize others over their own souls.
